children: Wall Street is bracing for potential volatility Friday as more than $2T in options are set to expire in a quarterly event with a notoriously punitive track record, according to Bluekurtic Market Insights.

Friday marks the arrival of "triple witching"—the simultaneous expiration of stock options, stock index options and stock index futures. Data tracking performance since 2000 reveals a rather consistent trend: the S&P 500
has ended the event day in negative territory 12 out of 14 times since 2012.
The only two exceptions during that span occurred in 2017 and 2025, when the index managed to eke out meager gains of 0.2% and 0.5%, respectively.
With over $2T in delta notional options expiring at once, market watchers are warning that the quarterly liquidity event could spark downward movement.
The looming expiration arrives against the backdrop of a month that is historically
on the calendar for equity markets. While the S&P 500
has managed to defy those seasonal headwinds so far with an uncharacteristically calm 0.3% gain, Friday's massive expiration event could prove to be the ultimate test for the month-to-date move.

title: S&P 500 faces $2T 'triple witching' threat Friday
